newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures fall on pre-weekend profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures fall on pre-weekend profit taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures ended lower across the board Friday in a moderate session, undermined by softer cash and some pre-weekend profit taking after recent gains, industry sources said.
October tumbled 9.8 cents to close at $1.965 per million British thermal units. November settled eight cents lower at $2.177. Other deferreds ended down by one to 6.3 cents.

"There was a lack of market (buyers) and there was some pre-weekend liquidation because of the Jewish holiday (Yom Kippur) Monday," said one Houston-based trader, adding Gulf cash was off slightly for the weekend.

While fairly wide cash-to-futures spreads may ensure healthy storage injections for the rest of this month, traders said builds next month should slow as caverns fill, backing more supply into the market and likely pressuring the cash.
Technically, traders pegged October support at $1.95 and then in the $1.88-1.885 gap. Resistance was seen at $2.10.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices eased one to two cents Friday to the mid-to-high $1.80s, with swing gas at the Hub talked just over $1.90. Midcon pipes fell a few cents to the low-$1.70s. New York city gate gas was off almost five cents to the $2.05-2.10 area on mild weather in the region.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip slipped 4.6 cents to $2.108. NYMEX said 41,979 Henry Hub contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 60,363.
NYMEX October Permian natgas closed five cents lower at $1.69, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 55 Permian contracts traded versus 15 on Thursday.
NYMEX October Permian natgas expires Thursday, Sept 26.

On the KCBT, October finished seven cents lower at $1.74, while deferreds ended down by two to seven cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.8 cents to 22.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 396 lots traded, up from Thursday's total of 263.
KCBT October natgas expires Wednesday, Sept 25.
